sources_considered.why: Dated primary benchmark report with low completion rates on complex software tasks and explicit guidance to retain human review.
Read the original September version to check the benchmark's scope and provenance. Its findings duplicate the cited benchmark report.
Read failure-analysis passages to check the original study. Not counted as independent corroboration of the same benchmark.
Contemporaneous primary evaluation provides material qualification: models can produce valuable work, while its one-shot comparisons do not establish repeated-task reliability.
Read the research summary, but did not rely on it for a dated quantitative reliability estimate.
Read relevant capability claims. A selected long-running demonstration does not establish general reliability, and publication was on the same day as the post.
Search results describe later model evaluations. They cannot directly establish the September 2025 state.

evidence_items.locator: Results: SWE-Bench Verified vs. SWE-Bench Pro; private commercial subset
evidence_items.explanation: The September benchmark report found that leading models completed only a small minority of complex private-codebase tasks under the tested setup. This supports the warning against assuming correct autonomous completion of such work.

GDPval supplies a material qualification: models produced competitive work across professional tasks. Its expert-preference comparisons and one-shot design do not establish consistent correctness over repeated runs.

unresolved_gaps: The evidence does not estimate reliability across the entire distribution of user requests.
These cited results do not measure repeated-run consistency for identical tasks.
No acceptable failure threshold was supplied by the speaker.
